effects.name: Typewriter
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI "typewriter" text view (iOS 17+). It reveals a string one character at a time at a fixed interval (default 60 ms), followed by a cursor character "|" in the accent color that blinks every 0.5 s. Implementation: keep a @State visibleCount, render Text(String(text.prefix(visibleCount))) concatenated with the cursor Text, and drive it from .task(id: text) with Task.sleep so it restarts when the text changes and cancels when the view disappears. Use the full text as the accessibility label.
effects.summary: Characters appear one by one with a blinking cursor.
effects.usage:
TypewriterText("Hello, SwiftUI!", interval: .milliseconds(60))
    .font(.title.bold())

effects.name: Scramble / Decode
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI "decode" text effect (iOS 17+). On appear, every character of the string is shown as a random glyph from a charset (A–Z, 0–9, #%&*), re-randomised every 30 ms. Over the given duration, characters lock into their real values from left to right until the full string is shown. Spaces never scramble. Use a monospaced font design so the width doesn't jitter, drive frames from .task(id: text) with Task.sleep, and set the real string as the accessibility label.
effects.summary: Random glyphs resolve into the real text from left to right.
effects.usage:
ScrambleText("ACCESS GRANTED", duration: 1.0)
    .font(.title.bold())

effects.name: Shimmer
effects.prompt: Create a reusable SwiftUI .shimmer() view modifier (iOS 17+). A soft white highlight band (a horizontal LinearGradient clear → white 80% → clear, about 35% of the view width) moves from just off the left edge to just off the right edge, repeating forever with linear timing (~1.6 s). The band is placed in an overlay with a GeometryReader and masked by the original content so it only lights up the view's own pixels (text glyphs or skeleton shapes). It must not intercept touches and should accept isActive, duration, bandWidth and highlight color parameters.
effects.summary: A band of light sweeps across text or skeleton placeholders.
effects.usage:
Text("Loading…")
    .font(.title)
    .shimmer()

RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8)
    .fill(.gray.opacity(0.3))
    .frame(height: 44)
    .shimmer(duration: 1.2)

effects.name: Gradient Sweep
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .gradientSweep(colors:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+) that paints a view's own pixels with a flowing multi-colour gradient. In an overlay, use a GeometryReader to draw a horizontal LinearGradient twice as wide as the view whose colours are the palette repeated twice plus the first colour again (so the right half matches the left half). Offset it from 0 to −width with a linear animation that repeats forever without autoreversing, so the loop is seamless. Mask the overlay with the original content so only glyphs or shapes are coloured, and disable hit testing. Default palette pink, orange, yellow, mint, cyan, purple over 3 s. With Reduce Motion on, show the gradient without moving it.
effects.summary: A multi-colour gradient flows through the letters forever.
effects.usage:
Text("Motion Library")
    .font(.largeTitle.weight(.heavy))
    .gradientSweep()

Image(systemName: "sparkles")
    .font(.system(size: 60))
    .gradientSweep(colors: [.yellow, .orange, .pink], duration: 2)

effects.name: Blur-in Words
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI BlurInText view (iOS 17+) that reveals a string piece by piece, split by word (default) or by character. Lay the pieces out with a custom Layout that flows left to right, wraps to new lines and centres each line; the gap between words is about 0.28 × the line height. Each piece starts at opacity 0, blur radius 8 and 8 pt lower, and animates to opacity 1, no blur and no offset with easeOut(0.6 s), delayed by index × stagger (0.08 s default). Replay when the text changes by resetting a revealed flag and setting it again on the next run loop. Expose the whole string as one accessibility label. With Reduce Motion on, only fade.
effects.summary: Words come into focus one after another: fade, rise and un-blur.
effects.usage:
BlurInText("Design is how it works.")
    .font(.title.weight(.semibold))

BlurInText("Letter by letter", by: .character, stagger: 0.03)

effects.name: Marquee
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI MarqueeText view (iOS 17+) for a single line of text. Measure the text's natural width (fixedSize text with a GeometryReader background) and the container width. If the text fits, show it still. If not, show two copies in an HStack separated by a gap (40 pt) and offset them left by (time × speed) modulo (textWidth + gap) using TimelineView(.animation), so the second copy takes the first copy's place and the loop is seamless. Speed defaults to 40 pt/s. Clip to the container and mask the edges with 16 pt linear fades. Reserve one line of height with a hidden copy of the text. Expose the full text to accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, don't scroll.
effects.summary: Text too long for its line scrolls sideways forever, with faded edges.
effects.usage:
MarqueeText("Now playing: Midnight Drive — Neon Coast")
    .font(.headline)
    .frame(width: 200)

MarqueeText(longTitle, speed: 60, gap: 24)

effects.name: Wave Text
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI WaveText view for iOS 18+ (mark it @available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)) that makes each letter bob up and down in a travelling wave while keeping normal text layout. Implement a TextRenderer whose draw(layout:in:) walks every line, run and glyph, keeps a running glyph index, copies the GraphicsContext, translates it vertically by sin((index / wavelength − time × speed) × 2π) × amplitude, and draws the glyph. Set displayPadding to the amplitude above and below so nothing clips. Drive time from TimelineView(.animation) and apply the renderer with .textRenderer. Defaults: amplitude 5 pt, wavelength 8 letters, 1 wave per second. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline and use zero amplitude.
effects.summary: Letters bob in a travelling wave, drawn with a TextRenderer.

effects.name: Pressable
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI ButtonStyle called PressableButtonStyle (iOS 17+). While pressed, the label scales to 0.94 and its brightness drops slightly (-0.06); on release it springs back using .spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.6). Fire a light impact haptic with .sensoryFeedback only when the press begins. Expose it as .buttonStyle(.pressable) and .buttonStyle(.pressable(scale:haptics:)) via a static extension on ButtonStyle.
effects.summary: Button squashes and darkens on press, then springs back with a light haptic.

effects.name: Tap Ripple
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .ripple() view modifier (iOS 17+) that shows a Material-style ripple. Use a simultaneous SpatialTapGesture so it doesn't block the view's own button action. Each tap appends a ripple at the tap location; each ripple is a translucent circle (white, 35% opacity) sized to 2× the view's diagonal that scales from ~0 to 1 while fading to 0 with easeOut over 0.7 s, then is removed. Ripples are drawn in an overlay clipped to a rounded rectangle with a configurable corner radius and never intercept touches. Multiple quick taps should produce overlapping ripples.
effects.summary: A circular ripple expands from the exact tap location.
effects.usage:
Text("Tap")
    .frame(width: 200, height: 60)
    .background(.indigo, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12))
    .ripple(color: .white, cornerRadius: 12)

effects.name: Error Shake
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .shake(trigger:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for error feedback. Every time the Equatable trigger changes, the view shakes horizontally using keyframeAnimator on an x offset: -10, +10, -7, +7, -3 points (≈0.07 s each, cubic keyframes) and then settles back to 0 with a bouncy SpringKeyframe. Amplitude should be configurable. Pair it with .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger:) for haptics.
effects.summary: Horizontal "no" shake for wrong input, triggered by a value change.

effects.name: Magnetic Button
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .magnetic(strength:radius:) view modifier (iOS 17+) that pulls a view toward the pointer. Pad the view by `radius` (60 pt) to enlarge its tracking area, give it a rectangular contentShape, measure the padded size with a GeometryReader background, then remove the padding again with .padding(-radius). In onContinuousHover (pointer on iPad, Mac and visionOS) and in a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) (touch), offset the original content by (location − centre) × strength (0.3) using an interactiveSpring(response 0.25, damping 0.7). When hover ends or the drag ends, spring back to zero with spring(response 0.45, damping 0.45) for a little overshoot. With Reduce Motion on, don't move.
effects.summary: The button drifts toward a nearby pointer or dragging finger, then springs home.
effects.usage:
Button("Get started") { }
    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    .magnetic()

Image(systemName: "plus.circle.fill")
    .font(.system(size: 44))
    .magnetic(strength: 0.5, radius: 40)

effects.name: Hold to Confirm
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI HoldToConfirmButton (iOS 17+) for destructive actions. A capsule with a 15% tint of fillColor (red) shows the label in fillColor. While pressed (onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration:perform:onPressingChanged:)), animate a progress value linearly from its current value to 1 over the remaining duration (1.2 s); releasing early animates it back to 0 with easeOut(0.35). Draw the liquid as a Shape filled from the bottom up to progress, with a sine-wave top edge (4 pt amplitude, phase driven by TimelineView) that flattens when empty or full. Mask a stack of the liquid plus a white copy of the label with the same shape, so the submerged part of the text turns white. On completion, run the action, swap the label for a checkmark with a spring, play a success haptic and reset after 1.2 s. Scale to 0.97 while pressing.
effects.summary: Liquid fills the button while you hold; the action runs only when it's full.

effects.name: Loading → Success
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI StatusButton (iOS 17+) driven by a status enum: idle, loading, success, failure. It is a 50 pt tall capsule Button. Idle shows the title at its natural width. For any other status the frame width animates to 50 pt, turning the capsule into a circle (spring response 0.45, damping 0.75), and the title shrinks and fades. Loading shows a white 70% arc spinning forever. Success turns the fill green and draws a white checkmark path with trim from 0 to 1 (easeOut 0.35 s, 0.15 s delay). Failure turns the fill red, scales in an xmark and shakes horizontally with a GeometryEffect (8 pt, three swings). Play success and error haptics with sensoryFeedback, disable the button when not idle, and expose the status as the accessibility value.
effects.summary: The button morphs into a spinner, then a green checkmark or a red shake.

effects.name: Glow Border
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .glowBorder(colors:cornerRadius:lineWidth:glowRadius:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+). In a non-interactive overlay, use TimelineView(.animation) to compute a rotation angle of (time / duration) turns (3 s per turn). Build an AngularGradient from the palette plus its first colour again (pink, purple, blue, cyan, mint by default) starting at that angle. Stroke a continuous RoundedRectangle with it twice: once at 2× line width, blurred by glowRadius (8) at 80% opacity for the glow, and once crisp at lineWidth (2). With Reduce Motion on, pause the rotation.
effects.summary: A rainbow border runs around the view with a soft glow behind it.
effects.usage:
Text("Upgrade to Pro")
    .padding()
    .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14))
    .glowBorder(cornerRadius: 14)

CardView()
    .glowBorder(colors: [.orange, .yellow], cornerRadius: 24, lineWidth: 3)

effects.name: Staggered Entrance
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .staggeredAppear(index:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for list and grid entrances. Each item starts at opacity 0, offset 24 pt down and scale 0.96, then on appear animates to its resting state with .spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.8), delayed by index × 0.08 s so the items cascade in. Delay per item and travel distance are configurable.
effects.summary: List items fade and rise into place one after another.
effects.usage:
ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
    CardView(item)
        .staggeredAppear(index: index)
}

effects.name: 3D Tilt
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .tiltOnDrag() view modifier (iOS 17+). While the user drags on the view, convert the drag translation into a normalised -1…1 value per axis (120 pt = full tilt) and apply two rotation3DEffects (x axis from vertical drag, y axis from horizontal drag) up to a max angle of ~12°, plus a 1.03 scale. Overlay a white glare gradient whose start/end points follow the tilt and which is only visible while dragging, clipped to the card's corner radius. Use .interactiveSpring while dragging and a bouncy spring back to flat on release.
effects.summary: Card tilts in 3D toward the finger with a moving glare, then springs flat.
effects.usage:
CardView()
    .tiltOnDrag(maxAngle: 15, cornerRadius: 20)

effects.name: Scroll Reveal
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .scrollReveal() view modifier (iOS 17+) using scrollTransition(.interactive). When an item is fully inside the scroll view (phase.isIdentity) it is at full opacity, scale 1 and no blur; as it moves toward the top or bottom edge it interpolates to opacity 0.3, scale 0.85 and a 2 pt blur. Axis, minimum scale, minimum opacity and blur amount should be parameters.
effects.summary: Rows scale up and come into focus as they enter the visible area.

effects.name: Flip Card
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI FlipCard<Front, Back> view (iOS 17+) with isFlipped and axis (horizontal or vertical) parameters and front/back view builders. Stack both faces in a ZStack and give each an Animatable view modifier holding the animated angle (0 or 180°). The back face uses angle − 180 so it reads correctly once turned. Each face applies rotation3DEffect around the y axis (or x for vertical) with perspective 0.5 and sets opacity to 1 only while |faceAngle| < 90°, so the faces swap exactly at the halfway point and the back never shows mirrored. Animate isFlipped changes with spring(response 0.6, damping 0.75). Hide the hidden face from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, cross-fade instead of rotating.
effects.summary: A two-sided card turns over in 3D with a spring.

effects.name: Swipe Card Stack
effects.prompt: Create a generic SwiftUI SwipeCardStack (iOS 17+) over a collection of Identifiable items with a card view builder and an onSwipe(item, direction) callback. Show the top 3 cards from the current position (looping by default). Cards behind are scaled down 5% per level and moved down 12 pt per level. The top card follows a DragGesture: offset by the translation, rotate by translation.width / 20 degrees around the bottom anchor, and overlay a green (right) or red (left) wash, masked by the card, whose opacity grows to 25% at the threshold. On release, if the predicted end translation passes 110 pt, fly the card 600 pt off in that direction with easeIn(0.25), then reset the drag without animation, advance the position with a spring so the pile moves up, and call onSwipe. Otherwise spring back. Add Swipe left and Swipe right accessibility actions.
effects.summary: Tinder-style deck: drag the top card away and the pile moves up.

effects.name: Parallax Carousel
effects.prompt: Create a generic SwiftUI ParallaxCarousel (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with an optional selection binding. Use a horizontal ScrollView with a LazyHStack (14 pt spacing), .scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), hidden indicators, .scrollPosition(id:anchor: .center), and horizontal contentMargins so each card (78% of the width) snaps to the centre with neighbours peeking. Draw each card's content wider than the card by the parallax factor (0.35), then use .visualEffect to read the card's frame in the .scrollView coordinate space and offset the content by −(distance of the card centre from the viewport centre) × parallax. Finally frame it to the card size and clip it with a continuous rounded rectangle (22 pt), so the image appears to move slower than its frame. With Reduce Motion on, set parallax to 0.
effects.summary: Paging cards whose images slide slower than the cards, for depth.
effects.usage:
ParallaxCarousel(places) { place in
    Image(place.photo)
        .resizable()
        .scaledToFill()
}
.frame(height: 240)

effects.name: Expandable Card
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI ExpandableCard<Header, Detail> (iOS 17+) bound to isExpanded. A VStack holds a plain-style Button containing the header, a spacer and a chevron.down that rotates −180° when open, then, if expanded, the detail view. Toggle inside withAnimation(.spring(response 0.45, damping 0.8)) so the card's height springs. Insert the detail with a combined transition of opacity, an 8 pt upward offset and a custom blur transition (radius 6 → 0). The background is a continuous rounded rectangle (16 pt) filled with the background style whose shadow deepens when open. Expose Expanded/Collapsed as the accessibility value. With Reduce Motion on, use a short ease and an opacity transition only.
effects.summary: Tap the header and the card springs open, un-blurring its detail.

effects.name: Pulse Rings
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI PulseRings view (iOS 17+). Draw N stroked circles (default 3, 2 pt line) that each grow from 20% to 100% of the frame while fading from opacity 1 to 0 over a 2 s cycle, evenly phase-offset so a new ring is always emerging. Drive it with TimelineView(.animation) and compute each ring's progress from the timeline date (no @State or repeatForever), so it never drifts and stops when off screen. Hide it from accessibility.
effects.summary: Concentric rings expand and fade continuously, like a radar or live dot.

effects.name: Like Burst
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .burst(trigger:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for "like" feedback. Every time the Equatable trigger changes (and isEnabled is true), spawn a burst in an overlay: 12 small circles (alternating 7 pt and 4 pt) placed evenly around a circle, which move outward from the centre to a ~36 pt radius while shrinking to 30% and fading out with easeOut over 0.6 s. Remove each burst after it finishes, allow overlapping bursts, and never intercept touches. Color, count and radius are parameters.
effects.summary: Particles fly outward from the centre when a value changes.
effects.usage:
Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
    .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
    .burst(trigger: isLiked, color: .pink, isEnabled: isLiked)

effects.name: Checkmark Draw
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI AnimatedCheckmark view (iOS 17+) with isChecked, color (green) and lineWidth (4 at 60 pt, scaled with size). It is square. Layer three parts in a ZStack: a circle stroke trimmed from 0 to 1 and rotated −90° so it draws clockwise from the top (easeInOut 0.45 s); a filled circle that scales from 0.6 and fades in with a spring after 0.35 s; and a white checkmark path (short stroke down-right, long stroke up-right, round caps and joins) trimmed from 0 to 1 with easeOut 0.3 s after 0.55 s. Finish with a small bouncy scale pop at 0.75 s. Unchecking reverses everything without delays. With Reduce Motion on, replace the sequence with a 0.2 s fade.
effects.summary: A success mark draws itself: circle stroke, fill, then a popping check.
effects.usage:
AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked: isDone)
    .frame(width: 80, height: 80)

AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked: saved, color: .blue, lineWidth: 3)

effects.name: Confetti
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .confetti(trigger:colors:count:spread:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Each change of the equatable trigger appends a burst with a start date and 80 random pieces, removed after 2.4 s. Each piece has a velocity fanned ±60° around straight up (speed up to 3.2 × spread), a spin rate, a wobble phase, a 5–9 × 8–14 pt size, a colour index and every fourth one is a circle. Draw all bursts in one Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), in an overlay enlarged by .padding(−spread) (160 pt) so confetti flies beyond the view, with hit testing off. Position = origin + velocity × (1 − e^(−1.6t)) / 1.6 + ½ × gravity × t² (air drag plus gravity), rotate by spin × t, scale x by cos(wobble + 8t) to fake turning over, and fade out over the last 0.6 s. With Reduce Motion on, skip the burst.
effects.summary: Confetti bursts out of the view, tumbles under gravity and fades.

effects.name: Loaders
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI MotionLoader view (iOS 17+) with a style enum (spinner, dots, bars, orbit, pulse), a color and a speed multiplier. It is square and drives everything from TimelineView(.animation) time, sizing parts relative to its side. Spinner: a round-capped arc whose trim length breathes between 15% and 75% while it rotates. Dots: three dots hopping up in sequence (max(0, sin(6t − i·0.9))) and brightening at the top. Bars: five capsules whose heights follow a sine wave offset per bar. Orbit: two dots circling each other, scaled and layered by a fake depth. Pulse: two rings expanding and fading in turn around a centre dot. Label it "Loading" for accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, show a dot that slowly breathes in opacity.
effects.summary: Five looping activity indicators: spinner, dots, bars, orbit and pulse.
effects.usage:
MotionLoader(.spinner)
    .frame(width: 32, height: 32)

MotionLoader(.dots, color: .secondary)
    .frame(width: 44, height: 44)

effects.name: Morphing Blob
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI MorphingBlob view (iOS 17+) generic over a ShapeStyle fill, with a convenience initializer taking colours for a diagonal LinearGradient. Draw a custom Shape in TimelineView(.animation): place N control points (6) evenly around the centre, each at radius base × (1 + wobble × (0.6·sin(1.1t + 1.7i) + 0.4·sin(0.7t + 2.9i))), where base = half the side × (1 − wobble) and wobble is 0.18. Connect them into a smooth closed curve with a Catmull-Rom spline converted to cubic Béziers (control points p1 + (p2 − p0)/6 and p2 − (p3 − p1)/6). Keep a 1:1 aspect ratio and hide it from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, freeze the shape.
effects.summary: An organic, lava-lamp blob whose outline never stops changing.
effects.usage:
MorphingBlob(colors: [.purple, .pink, .orange])
    .frame(width: 200, height: 200)

MorphingBlob(fill: Color.blue.opacity(0.3), points: 8, wobble: 0.1)
    .overlay(Image(systemName: "mic.fill"))

effects.name: Aurora
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI AuroraBackground view (iOS 17+). On a dark base color, draw one large circle per palette color (default purple, blue, teal, pink; 80% opacity, diameter 70% of the larger side). Each circle drifts on its own Lissajous path, x = cos(t·0.6 + phase)·30% width and y = sin(t·0.8 + phase·1.3)·30% height, where phase differs per index. Drive time from TimelineView(.animation) scaled by a speed parameter, blur the whole group with a ~60 pt radius, clip to bounds and hide it from accessibility.
effects.summary: Soft, blurred colour blobs drift slowly behind your content.

effects.name: Rolling Number
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI RollingNumber view (iOS 17+) that displays a number with odometer-style digit rolling. Render Text(value, format:) with monospacedDigit(), apply .contentTransition(.numericText(value:)) so digits roll up when the value increases and down when it decreases, and animate changes with .snappy. Provide initialisers for Int and for Double with a FloatingPointFormatStyle.
effects.summary: Digits roll like an odometer when the value changes.
effects.usage:
RollingNumber(value: score)
    .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))

effects.name: Particle Field
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI ParticleField view (iOS 17+) with count (50), color, speed (14 pt/s) and linkDistance (70 pt). Generate each particle's traits once from a seeded SplitMix64 generator: start position (0…1 in each axis), direction, speed factor (0.4–1.2), radius (1–2.8 pt) and opacity (0.4–1). In TimelineView(.animation) with a Canvas, compute each position as start + direction × time × speed × factor, wrapped around the canvas edges, so there is no stored state. Stroke a 0.8 pt line between every pair closer than linkDistance with opacity 0.35 × (1 − distance / linkDistance), then fill each particle as a circle. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, freeze time.
effects.summary: Drifting particles linked by faint lines, like a living constellation.

effects.name: Starfield
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI Starfield view (iOS 17+) with count (200), speed (0.35 depth units per second) and color. Give each star a seeded random x and y in −1…1 and a depth in 0…1. In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), compute z = 0.05 + 0.95 × fract(depth − time × speed), so stars approach the camera and wrap back to the far plane. Project with perspective: point = centre + (x, y) / z × 0.15 × half the larger side. Draw each star as a round-capped streak from its projection at a slightly larger z (z + min(0.08, speed × 0.05)) to its current projection, with opacity and line width growing as it gets closer. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, freeze time.
effects.summary: Stars stream out of the centre and stretch into streaks: warp speed.
effects.usage:
Starfield()
    .background(.black)
    .ignoresSafeArea()

Starfield(count: 300, speed: 1.5) // warp jump

effects.name: Cover Flow
effects.prompt: Create a generic SwiftUI CoverFlow carousel (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with an optional selection binding, itemWidth (140), spacing (−10) and maxAngle (50°). Use a horizontal ScrollView + LazyHStack with .scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), hidden indicators, .scrollPosition(id:anchor: .center) and contentMargins that centre the first and last items. In .visualEffect, read the item's frame in the .scrollView coordinate space, compute p = clamp((midX − viewport centre) / itemWidth, −1, 1) and apply rotation3DEffect of −p × maxAngle around the y axis (perspective 0.6), scale 1 − |p| × 0.18 and brightness −|p| × 0.25. Raise the selected item's zIndex. With Reduce Motion on, drop the rotation.
effects.summary: Side items turn away in 3D, shrink and dim; the centre faces you.
effects.usage:
CoverFlow(albums) { album in
    Image(album.artwork)
        .resizable()
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12))
}
.frame(height: 220)

effects.name: Float 3D
effects.prompt: Create a SwiftUI .float3D(height:angle:period:shadow:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Inside TimelineView(.animation), let t = time × 2π / period (3 s) and lift = 0.5 + 0.5·sin t. Rotate the content in 3D by sin(t/2) × angle (12°) around the y axis and cos(0.7t) × angle/2 around the x axis (perspective 0.5), and move it up by height (10 pt) × lift. Behind it, at the bottom, draw a black ellipse 12 pt tall, 18 pt below, that gets lighter (opacity 0.25 − 0.1·lift), narrower (scale x 0.75 − 0.15·lift) and blurrier (6 + 4·lift) as the view rises. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline.
effects.summary: The view hovers: a gentle bob, a slow 3D sway and a breathing shadow.
effects.usage:
Image("product")
    .resizable()
    .scaledToFit()
    .frame(width: 180)
    .float3D()

BadgeView()
    .float3D(height: 6, angle: 8, period: 4, shadow: false)

install:
```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library", branch: "main")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "MotionLibrary", package: "SwiftUI-Motion-Library")
```

Then `import MotionLibrary`. Requires iOS 17, macOS 14 or visionOS 1; effects marked iOS 18+ are `@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)`.
